page.text:
Residues represent the ultimate distillation of local singularity
structure into a single complex number detected by closed contour
integration. Because all powers $(z - z_0)^n$ with $n \ne -1$ possess
single-valued primitives $(z - z_0)^{n+1}/(n+1)$ along loops, they
contribute identically zero to any closed path integral.

Only the power $(z - z_0)^{-1}$ generates a non-trivial topological
winding period $2\pi i$ due to the branching of the complex logarithm
$\log(z - z_0)$. The Residue Theorem is therefore the triumphant
local-to-global bridge of complex analysis: it reduces the global
evaluation of contour integrals along arbitrary closed paths to a finite
algebraic sum of local residues.
